findings.claim: The new guard only prevents a direct self-cycle (`parent === mockPrototype`). It misses an indirect cycle, where `mockPrototype` already appears further up `parent`'s prototype chain. In that case `Object.setPrototypeOf` still throws `TypeError: Cyclic __proto__ value`.
findings.rationale: Take an implementation whose `prototype` inherits from the mock's prototype, such as `class Sub extends mockFn {}` followed by `mockFn.mockImplementation(Sub)`. Then `Sub.prototype !== mockPrototype`, so the guard passes, but `mockPrototype` is on `Sub.prototype`'s chain. Setting `mockPrototype`'s parent to `Sub.prototype` creates a cycle and throws. A complete guard would be `parent !== mockPrototype && !Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf.call(mockPrototype, parent)`, or it would skip reparenting whenever `mockPrototype` is in `parent`'s chain.
